exercises.heading: 6.3. Exercises

problem.paragraph: Let $$S$$ be the solid obtained by rotating the region shown in the figure about the $$y$$ -axis. Explain why it is awkward to use the washer method to find the volume $$V$$ of $$S$$ . Sketch a typical approximating shell. What are its circumference and height? Use shells to find $$V$$ .

image.alt: Details A curve and a shaded region are graphed on the first quadrant of the x y coordinate plane. The x axis has a single tick mark labeled 1. The curve, labeled y = x(x minus 1)^2, begins from the origin, goes up to the right, concaves down, reaches a high point and goes down to the right gradually to meet the x axis at (1, 0). The region under the curve and above the x axis is shaded.

problem.paragraph: Let $$S$$ be the solid obtained by rotating the region shown in the figure about the $$y$$ -axis. Sketch a typical cylindrical shell and find its circumference and height. Use shells to find the volume of $$S$$ . Is this method preferable to using washers?

image.alt: Details A curve and a shaded region are graphed on the first quadrant of the x y coordinate plane. The x axis has a single mark labeled sqrt(pi). The curve, labeled y = sin(x^2), begins from the origin, goes up to the right, gradually at first, concaves up, and then more rapidly, concaves down, reaches a high point, goes down to the right to meet the x axis at (sqrt(pi), 0). The region under the curve and above the x axis is shaded.

exercises.instruction: 3–4 A solid is obtained by rotating the shaded region about the specified line. Set up an integral using the method of cylindrical shells for the volume of the solid. Evaluate the integral to find the volume of the solid.

image.alt: Details A curve and a shaded region are graphed on the first quadrant of the x y coordinate plane. The x axis has a single tick mark labeled sqrt(pi)/2 and the y axis has a single tick mark labeled 1. The curve labeled y = cos(x^2), begins from (0, 1), runs horizontally, and then goes down to the right, concaves down, and meets the x axis at (sqrt(pi)/2, 0). The region under the curve and above the x axis is shaded.

Details A curve, a line, and a shaded region are graphed on the first quadrant of the x y coordinate plane. The x axis is displayed from 0 to 2 and the y axis from 0 to 1, both in increments of 1. The curve, y = sqrt(x), begins from the origin, goes up to the right, concaves down, rapidly at first and then more gradually, and exits at the top right. The line, y = 2 minus x, slopes downward to the right, crosses the curve at (1, 1), meets the x axis at (2, 0), and exits at the top left. The region bound by the curve and the line, above the x axis, is shaded.

image.alt: Details A curve and a shaded region are graphed on the first quadrant of the x y coordinate plane. The x axis has a single tick mark labeled 4. The region under the curve and above the x axis is shaded.

Details Two curves and a shaded region are graphed on the first quadrant of the x y coordinate plane. The first curve is labeled y = sqrt(x), begins at the origin, goes up to the right, concaves down passes through the point (1, 1), and exits at the top right. The second curve is labeled y = x^3, briefly runs along the x axis, then goes up to the right, concave up, and passes through (1, 1) while crossing the first curve, runs below the first curve, and exits at the top right. The region bound by the two curves is shaded.

exercises.instruction: 25, 26, 27, 28, 29, and 30 Use the method of cylindrical shells to find the volume generated by rotating the region bounded by the given curves about the specified axis.

problem.paragraph: Use the Midpoint Rule with $$n = 5$$ to estimate the volume obtained by rotating about the $$y$$ -axis the region under the curve $$y = \sqrt{1 + x^{3}}$$ , $$0 \leqslant x \leqslant 1$$ .
If the region shown in the figure is rotated about the $$y$$ -axis to form a solid, use the Midpoint Rule with $$n = 5$$ to estimate the volume of the solid.

The x axis is displayed from 0 to 10 in increments of 2 and the y axis is displayed from 0 to 4 in increments of 2. The loop passes through the approximate points (0, 3), (1, 4), (3, 5), (5, 4), (6, 3.6), (7, 4), (8, 4.25), (9, 4), (10, 3), (9, 2), (8, 1.8), (7, 2), (4, 1.5), (3, 1), (1, 2) and reaches (0, 3) once again. exercises.instruction: 39, 40, 41, and 42 Each integral represents the volume of a solid. Describe the solid.

solution.paragraph: Solid obtained by rotating the region $$0 \leqslant y \leqslant x^{4}$$ , $$0 \leqslant x \leqslant 3$$ about the $$y$$ -axis
Solid obtained (using shells) by rotating the region $$0 \leqslant x \leqslant 1 \slash y^{2}$$ , $$1 \leqslant y \leqslant 4$$ about the line $$y = - 2$$

exercises.instruction: 43–44 Use a graph to estimate the $$x$$ -coordinates of the points of intersection of the given curves. Then use this information and a calculator or computer to estimate the volume of the solid obtained by rotating about the $$y$$ -axis the region enclosed by these curves.
45–46 Use a computer algebra system to find the exact volume of the solid obtained by rotating the region bounded by the given curves about the specified line.

image.alt: Details A curve, a line, and a shaded region are graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The curve, y = 1/(1 + x^2), enters from the top left, crosses the y axis, goes down to the right gradually, initially concave down and then concave up, and exits at the bottom right. The line y = x/2 enters from the bottom left crosses the origin, rises upward to the right, crosses the curve at a point labeled (1, 1/2), and exits at the top right. The region between the x axis, the curve, and the line is shaded.

Details Two curves and a shaded region are graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The first curve is labeled y = 2 minus x^2, enters from the top left, crosses the y axis, goes down to the right, concave down, and exits at the bottom right. The second curve is labeled y = x^2, enters from the bottom left, crosses the y axis at the origin, briefly runs along the x-axis, then goes up to the right, concave up, crosses the first curve, and exits at the top right. The region is bound by the two curves and the y axis is shaded.

Details A curve is graphed in the first quadrant of the x y coordinate plane. The x axis has a single tick mark labeled pi. The curve y = sqrt(sin(x)) begins at the origin, traces an arch resembling a semicircle, and meets the x axis at pi. The region under the curve and above the x axis is shaded.

Details A curve, a line, and a shaded region are graphed on the first quadrant of the x y coordinate plane. The curve, y = 4x minus x^2 is a parabola opening downward with its left arm passing through the origin. The line y = x enters from the bottom left, passes through the origin and crosses the right arm of the parabola, and exits at the top right. The region bound by the curve and the line is shaded.

Details Two curves, a line segment, and a shaded region are graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The x axis has a single tick mark labeled 1/2, to the right of the origin. The first curve is labeled y = x^2, enters from the bottom left, runs along the x axis as it passes through the origin, then goes up to the right, concave up, and exits at the top right of the viewing window. The second curve is labeled y = x^3, enters from the bottom left, runs along the x axis a bit further than the first curve, then goes up to the right more gradually than the first curve, concaves up, and exits at the top right, below the first curve. A vertical line segment directly above x = 1/2 connects both curves. The region is bound by the two curves and the line segment is shaded.

Details A curve, a line, and a shaded region are graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The x axis has a single tick mark labeled 2. The curve, x = 3y minus y^2 is a parabola opening leftward with its bottom arm passing through the origin. The line x = 2 runs vertically passing through the tick mark 2 on the x axis and cutting the tip of the parabola. The region bound by the curve and the line is shaded.

exercises.instruction: 53, 54, 55, 56, 57, 58, and 59 The region bounded by the given curves is rotated about the specified axis. Find the volume of the resulting solid by any method.

problem.paragraph: Let $$T$$ be the triangular region with vertices $$(0,0)$$ , $$(1,0)$$ , and $$\left( {1,2} \right)$$ , and let $$V$$ be the volume of the solid generated when $$T$$ is rotated about the line $$x = a$$ , where $$a > 1$$ . Express $$a$$ in terms of $$V$$ .

exercises.instruction: 61, 62, and 63 Use cylindrical shells to find the volume of the solid.

problem.paragraph: A right circular cone with height $$h$$ and base radius $$r$$

Suppose you make napkin rings by drilling holes with different diameters through two wooden balls (which also have different diameters). You discover that both napkin rings have the same height $$h$$ , as shown in the figure.

list.item: Guess which ring has more wood in it.

Check your guess: use cylindrical shells to compute the volume of a napkin ring created by drilling a hole with radius $$r$$ through the center of a sphere of radius $$R$$ and express the answer in terms of $$h$$ . Details The figure has two parts, both parts are three-dimensional renderings of spheres with a cylindrical space at their centers and a height h. The first sphere and its central cylindrical space are narrow. The second sphere is broader than the first sphere with a broader cylindrical space at its center.
